method.label: Find a candidate and verify it

annotationRationale: Two particular lines determine the unique candidate, and the arithmetic-mean identity verifies that it belongs to every line.
sourceMethod: Followed the official third method: use the coefficient triples (0,1,2) and (1,0,-1), then verify the candidate using equal differences.

review.mathCheck: The valid progressions (0,1,2) and (1,0,−1) force y=2 and x=−1. Every progression satisfies c=2b−a, so substituting (−1,2) gives ax+by=−a+2b=c. This proves existence and uniqueness, yielding A.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, originally worded adaptation of the third approach in numbered MAA solution 4, continued on the second supplied page: intersect two convenient family members and verify the arithmetic-progression identity.
review.annotationCheck: The two assessed nodes match both substantive steps. Substitution is routine background; its omission as a separate node is not material.
